title: Rezera revs up for $181M IPO to fund phase 3 trial of NLRP3 inhibitor
summary: Rezera—the new name for NodThera—is aiming for a $181 million IPO to take its NLRP3 inhibitor into phase 3 trials for a cardiovascular disease.

title: MetaVia sees GLP-1 shed liver fat and body weight in phase 1, takes aim at specific liver disease
summary: MetaVia has linked its GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist to reductions in liver fat and body weight in a phase 1 trial. Encouraged by the data, MetaVia plans to start a phase 2 trial in alcohol-associated liver disease next year.

title: AstraZeneca said to offer $10B to acquire Rhythm, analysts whisper of a bidding war
summary: AstraZeneca has made a roughly $10 billion offer to purchase rare obesity disease player Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, The Wall Street Journal reports. At least three teams of analysts suggest a bidding war could be brewing and that Rhythm is unlikely to settle for AZ’s current pitch.

title: Agios aims to shed over 100 R&D roles this year ahead of hoped-for sickle cell disease approval
summary: Agios Pharmaceuticals has been shrinking its R&D headcount over the course of 2026 as the commercial-stage company looks to eliminate more than 100 roles by year-end.

title: Cash-strapped Vivoryon regains China rights to kidney disease prospect from Simcere
summary: Vivoryon Therapeutics has regained the China rights to its kidney disease prospect as the German biotech’s cash reserves begin to dry up.

title: Evommune signs $1B deal with China’s Hinova to enter same molecular glue niche as Novartis
summary: Evommune has paid $30 million to China’s Hinova Pharmaceuticals to get stuck into a niche of preclinical molecular glue degrader development that’s also being pursued by Novartis.

title: T-Therapeutics raises $133M series B for bispecific pipeline with Big Pharma backers in tow
summary: T-Therapeutics has pulled in a $133 million series B financing round that will be used to fund the biotech’s lineup of T cell receptor CD3 bispecific drug candidates.

title: Cloudbreak posts phase 3 eye disease win amid IPO storm
summary: A phase 3 study of Cloudbreak Pharma’s eye disease drug candidate has hit its co-primary endpoints, boosting a biotech embroiled in an IPO investigation.

title: Charles River teams up with Ipsen to use virtual control groups in toxicology studies
summary: Charles River Laboratories’ virtual control group (VCG) database will be used in a toxicology study run by French biopharma company Ipsen.

title: Madrigal’s former clinical development head files whistleblower lawsuit alleging Rezdiffra safety cover-up
summary: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals is facing a whistleblower lawsuit alleging that senior leadership censored serious liver-injury data related to its breakthrough MASH drug Rezdiffra and retaliated against the firm’s top clinical development head who tried to sound the alarm.

title: Smith+Nephew held failed talks with J&J over potential orthopedics combination
summary: Smith+Nephew held talks with Johnson & Johnson’s hip-and-knee replacement unit DePuy Synthes aimed at a potential combination with its orthopedics unit.

title: Minghui grants ASKA Japanese rights to sub-q TED candidate in $440M deal
summary: China’s Minghui Pharmaceutical has licensed its late-stage thyroid eye disease candidate to ASKA Pharmaceutical for up to $440 million, granting the Japanese drugmaker exclusive development and commercialization rights in its home country.

title: Blackstone Life Sciences teams up with Boston Scientific in $455M heart pump deal
summary: Blackstone Life Sciences has penned a $455 million collaboration with Boston Scientific to co-fund the development of the medtech’s next-generation miniature heart pump system.

title: Boehringer returns to Sino Biopharma in $7.4B deal for preclinical TCEs, ADCs
summary: Boehringer Ingelheim has returned to China to satisfy its appetite for antibody-drug conjugates and T-cell engagers.

title: nPhase rakes in $30M to expand AI-native clinical data platform
summary: Clinical research company nPhase has closed a $30 million series D financing round to expand its AI-native clinical data platform.

title: AbbVie pens $1.4B deal for deprioritized IBD drug from Nxera
summary: AbbVie has added another angle to its relationship with Nxera, with the Big Pharma paying $100 million upfront for a phase 1 inflammatory bowel disease candidate.

title: Ultragenyx shrinks workforce and axes assets to halve R&D spend
summary: Ultragenyx is laying off 20% of its workforce and axing drug development programs to cut its annual R&D budget to half of the amount it spent in 2025.

title: Sanofi scraps STAT6 degrader from Nurix just 2 months after entering clinic
summary: Sanofi has decided to end work on a STAT6 degrader from Nurix just two months after taking the inflammatory disease drug into the clinic.

title: Novo’s CEO still looking for deals to ‘close some of the gaps,’ as misfires hit profits
summary: Novo’s CEO has told Fierce that the company remains on the hunt for deals that “close some of the gaps” in its pipeline, as the Big Pharma reports billions of dollars in impairment charges from a string of recent clinical misses.

title: Servier’s $1.6B muscular dystrophy bet on Edgewise delivers quick-fire pivotal failure
summary: Servier’s decision to bet $1.55 billion on Edgewise Therapeutics’ muscular dystrophy program ahead of pivotal data has backfired. Five months after striking the deal, the French drugmaker has reported that a Becker muscular dystrophy trial missed its primary and secondary endpoints.

title: AbbVie invests £120M in UK, including expanded R&D site
summary: AbbVie is investing 120 million pounds ($160 million) to expand its U.K. R&D presence, in a show of faith in the country’s life sciences sector.

title: Insulin pump maker MiniMed names David Segal chief medical officer
summary: MiniMed has hired David Segal, M.D., as its new chief medical officer, bringing in a diabetes care and digital health veteran as the company enters its next chapter as an independent business.

title: Philips sets aside $322M for proposed DOJ settlement over sleep apnea device recall
summary: Philips’ Respironics division has reached an “agreement in principle” with the U.S. Department of Justice to settle a long-running investigation into its recall of potentially defective sleep apnea devices.

title: The human claustrum tracks uncertainty and prediction error
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02471-1Single-neuron recordings provide direct evidence that the human claustrum tracks uncertainty and prediction errors during adaptive behavior. Its responses differed from those in the anterior cingulate cortex, which raises the possibility that these regions make distinct contributions to updating beliefs and guiding behavior in ever-changing environments.

title: Single-neuron encoding of rapidly learned visual information reshapes human perception
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02496-6The authors show that rapid learning modulates neuronal activity in the human visual cortex, requiring extra processing time to support recognition and relaying signals to memory-related regions without requiring feedback.

title: Estrogen Exposure Shields the Aging Brain
summary: Does lifetime estrogen protect the brain's microcirculation? A 5-year MRI study in Neurology reveals that a longer reproductive lifespan and hormone therapy use cut cerebral small vessel disease burden by up to 59%, preserving white matter integrity into older age.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, AAN, Aging, brain research, cerebral blood flow, cognition, estrogen, hormone replacement therapy, HRT, neurobiology

title: The Acoustic Science of What Makes a Great Singer
summary: What separates a good opera singer from a great one in the ears of competition judges? Keio University researchers simulated a live vocal competition, revealing that the 2–4 kHz "singer’s formant" and sex-specific vibrato tuning drive top marks, while raw loudness matters little.
category: Auditory Neuroscience, Featured, Neuroscience, acoustics, auditory neuroscience, brain research, Keio University, neurobiology, singers, vocalists

title: How Octopuses Lock in Long-Term Memory Without New Proteins
summary: How does an octopus hold onto memories without the molecular machinery used by humans? Researchers discovered a self-sustaining nitric oxide switch in the octopus vertical lobe that locks in long-term potentiation without requiring new protein synthesis.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, LTP, Memory, neurobiology, nitric oxide

title: Enriched Environments Rewire the Brain via Shared Synaptic Gene Networks
summary: How does an active, stimulating lifestyle physically rewire the brain? A meta-analysis of over 300 studies identifies a conserved molecular signature driven by the AP-1 transcription factor, unveiling the genomic machinery behind environmental enrichment.
category: Featured, Genetics, Neuroscience, brain research, environmental neuroscience, neurobiology, neuroplasticity, Psychology, synaptic plasticity, UMH

title: Glioblastoma’s Chaos Follows Predictable Rules
summary: Is glioblastoma's deadly chaos actually predictable? Researchers analyzed over one million tumor cells to uncover the hidden rules governing brain cancer plasticity, using AI to identify molecular switches that reprogram malignant cells into harmless states.
category: Brain Cancer, Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, brain research, Cancer, EMBL, glioblastoma, neurobiology

title: One Autism Mutation Collapses the Whole Gene Network
summary: How can hundreds of different mutations cause autism? Boston Children's Hospital researchers discovered "transcriptomic convergence"—where mutating one autism gene drags down a whole network—and identified ZFX, an X-linked gene that protects females from the collapse.
category: Autism, Featured, Genetics, Neuroscience, ASD, Boston Children's Hospital, brain development, brain research, developmental neuroscience, neurobiology, neurodevelopment

title: Why Bitter Coffee Starts to Taste So Good to Your Brain
summary: Why do we learn to love the bitter taste of coffee? A study in Nature led by UCSF reveals an internal "slow" dopamine circuit connecting gut nutrient sensors to the left amygdala, building over minutes to link post-ingestive caloric rewards with new flavors.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, amygdala, bitter taste, brain research, dopamine, gustatory neuroscience, neurobiology, taste perception, UCSF

title: Omega-3 DHA Eases Autism Behaviors by Calming Inflammation
summary: Can omega-3 fatty acids reshape brain circuits in autism? A study in Pediatric Discovery demonstrates that DHA reduces repetitive behaviors and restores sociability in early-stress rat models by blocking the prefrontal JNK inflammatory cascade and boosting NRF2 antioxidant enzymes.
category: Autism, Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, ASD, Autsim, behavioral neuroscience, brain research, Chinese Academy of Science, DHA, neurobiology, neuroinflammation, Omega 3, supplimentation

title: Neuromorphic Chip Decodes Brain’s Emotion Waves
summary: Can wearable brain monitors track emotions without draining batteries? Beijing Institute of Technology researchers developed a neuromorphic spiking neural network and asynchronous accelerator that decodes emotional states from EEG in 18 microseconds, using 97.5% less energy than conventional AI.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, emotion, neurobiology, Neurosceince, Neurotech, Science China Press

title: How Video Gamers Make Split-Second Decisions
summary: Can 5,000 hours of Counter-Strike sharpen your real-world reflexes? University of Sheffield researchers tested over 300 players, discovering a 90-millisecond mental processing edge in visual decision speed, but zero advantage in multitasking.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, decision making, gaming, neurobiology, Neurology, processing speed, University of Sheffield, visual processing

title: The Dark Side of Bonding With AI Companions
summary: Can a software update break a human heart? A study shows that while people find comfort in AI companions, they suffer acute anxiety and vulnerability fearing developers will alter or erase their digital partners.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, AI, Artificial Intelligence, bonding, brain research, emotion, LLMs, neurobiology, University of Surrey

title: Menopause Blood Protein Signature Tied to Dementia Risk
summary: How does menopause shape long-term brain health? A new study of 12,000 women reveals that a panel of 16 blood proteins linked to brain aging surges during the menopause transition, offering a midlife window to screen for future dementia risk.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, Aging, brain research, dementia, menopause, neurobiology
